title: Decision register additions — round 2 (price authority, staking, settlement)

rows.question: Which price source is authoritative for the market open and close snapshots in the price-snapshot store?
rows.why_it_matters: The market line and difference columns, closing line value, and demotion trigger G-D1.T3 all depend on it. Until it is answered those columns stay blank by rule.
rows.information_we_have: No official league source publishes betting prices (flag F-06). A community mirror (nflverse/nfldata) publishes single snapshots and historical initial/closing lines with no named book provenance (flag I-10). The store captures our own numbers correctly today.
rows.information_missing: An owner-approved price feed: a named sportsbook, a consensus definition, or an accepted community source with known provenance.
rows.how_to_get_it: Decide between: (A) subscribe to a licensed odds feed (e.g. a book API or an odds aggregator) and record its name in the source registry; (B) adopt the community mirror as a labelled benchmark with explicit acceptance of its provenance gap; (C) originate prices ourselves and treat our own numbers as the market column. Record the choice on the suggestion board.
rows.blocks_decision: yes — price store market columns, CLV trigger T3, edge/EV publication

rows.question: What staking plan does the leaderboard track (flat units, fractional Kelly, tiered), and what is the unit size?
rows.why_it_matters: The staking scorecard is deliberately unranked; it cannot become a decision tool until a plan exists. It also feeds the drawdown demotion trigger G-D1.T4.
rows.information_we_have: Signal metrics are staking-blind (flat 1-unit reference) and already ranked on. Per-bet series support drawdown and streak computation under any plan.
rows.information_missing: The owner's risk appetite: allocation size, maximum exposure per bet, and whether Kelly fractions are acceptable.
rows.how_to_get_it: Choose on the suggestion board (paths in SS-06 area of the suggestions page): flat 1% units (recommended default), quarter-Kelly on the model edge, or tiered stakes by gate confidence. Any choice is pre-registered before the next graded bet.
rows.blocks_decision: yes — staking scorecard values, G-D1.T4 threshold calibration

rows.question: What is the settlement authority and grading window for the verified results feed?
rows.why_it_matters: Automated grading and ROI publication need a rule for when a result is final (the league can correct a stat line) and who may re-grade.
rows.information_we_have: The feed grades only from official NFL.com FINAL scores and reproduces the official standings exactly (32/32 clubs). Week 10 TNF is graded; the remaining 13 games are pending by rule.
rows.information_missing: A correction policy: how long after kickoff a league correction is honoured, and who may trigger a re-grade.
rows.how_to_get_it: Adopt the freshness/correction policy already drafted in data/audit/what_changed.json as the settlement policy, or amend it on the suggestion board. Then wire grading into the data-refresh workflow.
rows.blocks_decision: yes — automated grading job, leaderboard ROI publication

rows.question: How are leaderboard rewards funded and paid, and in what jurisdiction?
rows.why_it_matters: The reward formula is defined and gate-weighted, but a reward with no funding source or legality review cannot be paid. Nothing is implemented ahead of this decision.
rows.information_we_have: Reward = 1000 x ROI x min(1, bets/300) x confidence, gate-weighted; strategy-level accounting is ready.
rows.information_missing: Funding source, prize jurisdiction and compliance review, and whether rewards are monetary, points, or recognition-only.
rows.how_to_get_it: Owner decision; if monetary, a compliance review before the first live season. Recognition-only needs no review. Record the choice on the suggestion board (carried from Q-06/Q-25).
